evidence: Turner channa covered explicitly includes Nepali chānu roof, Kumauni chāno shed and Garhwali chān cowshed. These adjacent Nepal survey roof forms are compared with that attested roof family. The i-ending forms are provisionally grouped with this regional family; the neighbouring *channi covering family (4992) remains a morphological alternative.

Turner *channi covering explicitly records Bihari chānh/chānhī/chānhiyā thatch roof, Old Awadhi chāna and Punjabi chann thatched roof. These central/eastern survey roof responses fit that noun family, with deaspiration and local ch/s spellings retained. The link is a regional comparative assignment; channa 4989 is related but separately represented.

Turner rajju explicitly records regional rāž/raž/raz rope, Pahari raj̈ūṛī, and Hindi lej/lejur. The Maiya z/ź forms and Kaithal leju fit those documented developments of the same rope family. Survey responses with ambiguous y transcription are excluded.

Turner explicitly identifies Punjabi rassī as the source of the widespread Hindi/Bihari rassī/rasrī and Awadhi rasarī rope family. These Bagheli forms are treated as contact forms; the existing Hindi rassī node is used as a provisional nearby donor proxy, preserving its Punjabi ancestry. The exact regional path of transmission and the local expanded vowels remain uncertain.
